topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, contextualizes the lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Mutations, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer develops through a balance of intrinsic biological errors and environmental exposures, supported by global epidemiological and migration data.

topics.label: Carcinogenic Agents and Mechanisms of Initiation and Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore specific biological, chemical, and physical carcinogens alongside the mechanisms of direct DNA mutation, xenobiotic activation, chronic inflammation, and tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogen Exposure and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the laboratory, genomic, animal, and epidemiological approaches used to identify carcinogen signatures and evaluate the carcinogenic potential of compounds.

topics.label: Conclusion: Risk-Benefit Analysis of Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides a concluding summary of the lecture and addresses the real-world decisions involved in balancing carcinogen risks against practical benefits.
